# JAMX second CRC initial value — 2026-10-31 recording

Source: local recording of the 2026-10-31 11:22 pass (decoder session
`20261031_112206_010`). The receiver did not recognise this JAMX CRC initial
value at the time, so no image was written to disk.

`jamx_ssdv_20261031.b64` contains the 82 unmodified 223-byte image frames
(SCID 0x0322, VCID 1) of that recording, in reception order. The two
transmissions are image ID 2 (47 usable packets) and image ID 3
(a re-transmission of the same picture, 10 usable packets); both are
640x480, quality 3. The JPEG payloads of the two transmissions are identical,
so the passes can be merged offline.

The stream validates with the CRC initial value `0xF87754B4`, a second value
used by JAMX in addition to `0x6AAAC1C5` (see `JAMX_14907288.md`). Neither
value is a callsign encoding: SSDV callsigns are 6 characters in base 40
(`0x00000000` - `0xF423FFFF`), and the DSLWP value `0x4EE4FDE1` does not
decode to a callsign either. The `ssdv_receiver` test therefore expects the
stream to be attributed to JAMX, while a packet with a completely unknown
initial value is shown as `Unknown`.

The test also checks that a mid-stream frame with an unknown CRC cannot open
a session on its own; only a clean first packet (packet ID 0, MCU 0, offset 0)
may start an "Unknown" image.
